compatibility.destructive_changes: require a new major contract and an explicit migration
compatibility.rollback: every destructive migration requires a tested rollback or restore procedure

extraction_latch.design_decision: Named public.loader_extraction_latch and shaped with a loader discriminator so the loader family can share one relation, matching discogs-sql-loader's tableinator/extraction_latch.py startup probe: it checks LATCH_CANDIDATES (public.loader_extraction_latch first, graph.extraction_latch second) against information_schema, requires the five non-key columns at their exact information_schema types, and — when the relation carries a loader column — keys and scopes every statement on it (its own _key_columns() and ON CONFLICT (loader, version)). Declaring the loader column and the composite primary key here up front means the loader's repin needs no statement changes, only removing its own candidate-name tolerance.
extraction_latch.note: A durable, per-(loader, extraction) latch recording which of a loader's entity types have signalled one extraction's `extraction_complete`, and whether that loader's post-import derived-relation refresh has completed for it (`refreshed_at`). Written before the triggering delivery is acked, so a restart resumes signal collection instead of losing it. Mirrors graphinator's Neo4j-side latch. This repository writes no row; discogs-sql-loader is the writer today, and musicbrainz-sql-loader may write its own (loader, version) rows into the same relation when it adopts the same pattern.

bootstrap.note: A one-off fill deriving every loader-written table from the catalog documents, using the same definitions those relations published as views before they were tables. It is NOT authoritative: the owner recorded against each relation writes it and supersedes this fill on its first pass. It exists so an environment can be populated once, before a loader has run, so a read rewrite is not blocked on the dual-write. Nothing calls it; applying the schema declares it and writes no row. Each relation is emptied and refilled in one transaction, so re-running converges in both directions and a row no document justifies is removed. It reports a row count per relation. One known divergence: a company with no Discogs id is keyed on its name case-folded, and this fill folds with SQL lower where the loader applies Python casefold, so a handful of characters key differently and the loader's row is the correct one.

counter_properties.note: graphinator writes these onto the Neo4j node of the same name, so the property graph publishes them on the same label rather than on a second one a rewrite would have to learn. SQL/PGQ admits one element table per label unless every table exposes an identical property set, so the label binds a view joining its storage relation to its counter relation; the counter relation is unique on the join column, so the planner removes the join for a query that reads no counter. A count reads zero where the loader has not computed one; first_year stays null. graph.release_degree is the one counter that stays a label of its own, because its live half is a pair of lateral counts no unique key makes removable.

key_columns.note: Every key column of every graph relation is text. PostgreSQL 19 beta 3 cannot resolve an equality operator for a character varying property-graph vertex key, so the four Discogs vertex views publish data_id::text and the loader-written tables are declared text from the start. This retires the graph.artist.artist_key, graph.label.label_key, graph.master.master_key, and graph.release.release_key restatements the phase 0 views appended for the same reason; nothing but CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH ever read them and they were never declared as properties.

graph_schema.note: Twenty relations are loader-written tables replacing a view that computed the same rows on every read, seven more hold the counters, degrees, and genre aggregates the graph enrichers compute today, and the rest are read-only views over tables declared elsewhere in this contract. This repository declares every one of them and writes rows into none: the owner named against each relation does that, so an empty table on a fresh database is the expected state rather than a fault.

property_graph.absent_on: PostgreSQL 18, and PostgreSQL 19 with the switch off
conditions: the SCHEMA_PROPERTY_GRAPH environment switch is enabled
property_graph.consumer_rule: consumers must not assume it exists; probe pg_class for a relation named catalog in schema graph, of relkind g, and fall back to the views, which are always present
property_graph.element_tables: Fifty-five of the sixty-four graph relations. The nine that bind no element hold rows or counters for a label that binds a view joining them, plus graph.release_degree_base, whose rows the graph reaches through graph.release_degree.
property_graph.name: graph.catalog
property_graph.note: A SQL/PGQ declaration over the graph schema's tables and views, applied after the rest of the PostgreSQL schema. A closed gate is logged and is not a failure. There is no IF NOT EXISTS for a property graph and this initializer never drops one except through a shape migration that re-declares it on the same run, so an existing graph.catalog is otherwise left as it is and a changed declaration does not roll out on its own.

view_evolution.allowed: appending a column to the end of an existing view
view_evolution.engine_enforcement: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW fails the statement outright rather than replacing the view
forbidden: renaming a view or a view column
view_evolution.migration: expand, migrate consumers, then contract, with a coordinated DROP ... CASCADE
view_evolution.shape_change: A relation that becomes a loader-written table is replaced by a guarded migration that drops the view only when one is still there, in the same pass that creates the table. The published column names survive the change; the key columns are retyped from character varying to text, which psycopg returns identically.

musicbrainz_delete_reconciliation.note: musicbrainz.relationships and musicbrainz.external_links were declared with created_at only, unlike every other MusicBrainz entity table. The additive updated_at column closes the gap: the loader refreshes it on every upsert and reconciles deletes by removing rows where updated_at < run start, the same purge_stale_rows shape discogs-sql-loader already runs against the Discogs entity tables' own updated_at. DDL ownership is database-schema alone, so this column is declared here rather than carried as a startup ALTER in the loader.
